sourceFacts.description: One thin hatched band extends across the bottom of the crop. Its upper boundary is nearly horizontal; its lower boundary is gently irregular/curved. There are two distinct interfaces, not a single reflecting line. Hatching identifies the intervening film, not a measured grid.
One unnumbered wavy stroke approaches from upper left, progresses downward/right, and reaches the upper surface at the leftmost junction. There is no printed incident-light label or measured angle.
The left outgoing wavy stroke leaves the incident junction on the outer surface and runs upward/right toward the eye. Its only printed label is 1, on the left of this outgoing path.

A second wavy outgoing stroke leaves a distinct upper-surface point to the right of the first junction and runs upward/right toward the same eye. Its printed label is 2, on the right of the second path. Short oblique strokes are visible within the hatched band near the two junctions; exact turning detail is partly obscured by the scan/hatching. The authoritative text resolves the topology: entry refraction, inner-surface reflection, exit refraction. No claim is made that exact internal angles can be read from these pixels.

One stylized eye with eyelid/lash-like strokes sits at the upper right. Both outgoing paths head into its vicinity, at separate locations. The crop does not establish a single focused intersection, retinal construction, observation-plane phase, or measured anatomical geometry.

No named points, normals, angle arcs, wavelength marks, thickness values, refractive indices, coordinates, phase labels, equations, color values, or subfigure letters appear. Wavy strokes are schematic wave identification, not measured crests or a specified optical phase. No source arrowhead is clearly resolved.

modernAdditionsAndLimits: Stable construction-point IDs and small junction dots are modern authoring aids; no point letters are displayed.
Locally flat parallel interfaces regularize the scanned film band; thickness is exaggerated to expose the path, not supplied as a physical measurement.
Air / Oil film / Water are English medium labels based on the current oil-on-water example, not labels read from the original pixels.
Wave 1 and Wave 2 retain the original numbered identities; Incident light, Eye, Outer surface and Inner surface are modern English labels.
Direction arrowheads are modern additions. The two outgoing paths remain distinct and are not forced to a false common focus.

The schematic wave wiggles do not encode wavelength, amplitude, coherence length or the total optical phase difference. No geometric-distance condition for bright/dark interference is placed on the image.
No interface phase reversal is assigned without index/polarization/model conditions. The complete current bilingual text supplies the conditional total-phase explanation.
The separate portrait tbl-p0226-01 and external color plates are not opened or authored.
